source.quote: Shanling's own announcement for the M3 Plus, read 2026-11-25; its product page is image-only, so this is the source. Verbatim: « -Hi-Res Support: PCM 32/768 & DSD512 »; « -DAC: Four CS43198 »; « -AMP: Two SGM8262 »; « -System: Open Android 13 ». A USB DAC mode is confirmed in prose and not quantified: « M3 Plus also matches our latest releases by adopting the modern open Android 13 system with AGLO Audio processing, two-way Bluetooth connectivity, USB DAC mode and USB Transport feature. »

_la_source_est_une_annonce_ou_un_manuel_: Shanling's product pages are image-only, so every figure comes from the maker's own announcement at /article/NNNNNN or from its manual PDF, both on en.shanling.com. No number was read off an image, and nothing is sourced to store.shanling.com. See the brand file.
_ni_DoP_ni_natif_ne_sont_dits_pour_ce_mo: DoP appears on no Shanling page or manual, and « native » only in the UA dongle manuals and in EM5. Neither is stated for this model.
_UN_SEUL_chiffre_et_le_fabricant_ne_dit_: The page gives one Hi-Res figure and never says whether it describes files played from the MicroSD card or a signal accepted at an input. On a portable player the headline figure is usually playback - the four old text pages, M0, M1, M2s and M3s, prove that this maker files it that way when it bothers to label it, and the EC Mini and EH3 label it « Local Playback » in so many words. So `pcm_max_hz` and `dsd_max` record what the device CONVERTS, which is true either way, and `inputs` is left empty rather than filled from a figure that may belong to a memory card. The ambiguity is the finding; resolving it would be inventing a fact.
